standard_prerequisites.name: Tautness of a continuous homomorphism of linearly topologized rings
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that the closure of IB is open for a weak ideal of definition I of A.

standard_prerequisites.name: The topologically nilpotent elements of a linearly topologized ring form a closed radical ideal, and the closure of the image of a set of topologically nilpotent elements consists of topologically nilpotent elements
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemma lemma-topologically-nilpotent, invoked at proof lines 1430-1431
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the closure of IB consists of topologically nilpotent elements, so it is a weak ideal of definition.

core_obligations: Choose a weak ideal of definition I of the weakly pre-admissible source A (proof lines 1428-1429).
Use tautness to see that the closure J of IB in B is open (proof lines 1429-1430).
Use the nilpotent-elements lemma to see that J consists of topologically nilpotent elements (proof lines 1430-1431).
Conclude that J is a weak ideal of definition of B, so that B is weakly pre-admissible (proof lines 1431-1432).
proof_roadmap: Choose the weak ideal of definition of the source (proof lines 1428-1429).
Openness of the closure of its extension by tautness (proof lines 1429-1430).
Nilpotence of the closure and conclusion (proof lines 1430-1432).
difficulty_reason: For a continuous homomorphism of linearly topologized rings that is taut with weakly pre-admissible source, the lemma asserts that the target is weakly pre-admissible (statement lines 1421-1426). The proof produces a weak ideal of definition of the target directly: a weak ideal of definition I of A is chosen, tautness gives that the closure J of IB is open, the earlier lemma on topologically nilpotent elements gives that J consists of topologically nilpotent elements, and therefore J is a weak ideal of definition of B (proof lines 1428-1433). The level is H2: the two ingredients (openness from tautness and the nilpotent-element description of the closure) are combined in a single displayed move, nothing is omitted.
